segments.role: A blocking-partner zone whose turnout does little for a change-led government and a great deal to keep Ra'am above the threshold and Netanyahu below 61.
segments.who: 38 Negev Bedouin localities hold 144,860 eligible voters; turnout was 51% in 2022 and Arab lists took 94% of the vote. Rahat (38,346 eligible, 61% turnout) is the largest, followed by Tel Sheva, Ar'ara BaNegev, Kuseife, Hura and Laqiya at 47-57%. About 40,000 voters in unrecognised villages vote at tribal stations 5-65 km from home, where turnout was 38% in 2022 against 56% in recognised towns.
segments.moves: Ra'am won about 74% of the Negev Arab vote in 2022, so Negev turnout drives much of its 78% chance of clearing the threshold. Crime, personal safety and real influence over the next government top Arab voters' concerns, and 77% back an Arab party joining the coalition. Distance is the binding constraint; tribal-station turnout rose from about 20% to 42% between the two 2019 elections, alongside volunteer transport and the Joint List's reunion.
segments.approach: Run no change-bloc-branded field work here. Turnout work belongs to Ra'am, local leaders and Arab civil-society coalitions, which already target low-turnout towns and reach voters through clan and community networks. Where the bloc supports that work, keep the support transparent, lawful under party-finance rules and separate from Jewish-sector campaigning. Any transport for tribal-station voters must run through a list or a registered body; the CEC chair ruled a 2019 busing plan political and let it proceed only if the group registered, so confirm with election counsel.
segments.message: Personal safety and an end to crime, with concrete plans on housing, jobs and services. Real influence over the next government gives the vote a purpose.
segments.messenger: Bedouin local leaders, Ra'am activists and Arabic-speaking civil-society volunteers from the community. Hebrew-speaking change-bloc canvassers should stay out.
segments.avoid: Never publicise turnout surges here or let change-bloc figures frame Arab votes as illegitimate; Likud plans to use the CEC's election-day station releases to rally its base, and delegitimising rhetoric can depress Arab turnout. Fund no rides, gifts or services of monetary value without written clearance from election counsel.

segments.role: A small blocking-partner zone with a real pocket of direct change-list votes, mainly for the Democrats.
segments.who: Six Christian-majority Galilee villages hold 27,005 eligible voters and turned out 59% in 2022. Arab lists took 76% and change-bloc predecessors 19%; the model projects change lists at 16% in 2026. Rameh (6,574 eligible, 26% projected change) is the one Secondary target, while Kafr Yasif, the largest village (8,257), projects 5%.
segments.moves: Meretz still held 11.7% in Christian villages in 2022, against 39.8% for Hadash-Ta'al. Crime and personal security lead Arab concerns. The Democrats are touring Arab towns, expanding Arabic social media and placed Somaya Bashir of Jatt 10th on their list.
segments.approach: Treat the segment as partner territory with one exception. The Democrats can canvass identified supporters in the polling stations the model marks positive in Rameh, Fassuta, Eilabun, Mi'ilya and Jish, where the projected change share is 18-26%, using Arabic-speaking local volunteers. Leave all other turnout work to Arab lists and civil society. Full saturation is worth about 4 net votes toward a change-led government and 146 toward blocking, so cap the investment.
segments.message: Personal security, equal services and Arab representation inside a governing list. For Blue and White and Reservists voters, a vote below the threshold is lost.
segments.messenger: Local Christian community figures and the Democrats' Arab candidates, speaking Arabic.
segments.avoid: Avoid any rhetoric that treats Arab votes as illegitimate, and keep direct appeals targeted and low-key. One weak 2019 experiment found no Jewish backlash to centre-left equality messaging aimed at Arab citizens, but Likud will use any visible Arab turnout surge to rally its base.

segments.role: The largest blocking-partner zone, holding 44% of the bloc's blocking potential and almost none of its change-government potential.
segments.who: 89 Arab localities in the Galilee and the Triangle hold 671,826 eligible voters; turnout was 54% in 2022 and Arab lists took 93%. The reservoir sits in large low-turnout towns such as Nazareth (59,519 eligible, 48%), Umm al-Fahm (38,286, 38%), Baqa al-Gharbiyye (48%) and Shefa-'Amr (51%). Sakhnin (68%), Tamra (64%) and Tira (62%) are already among the highest-turnout Arab towns.
segments.moves: Arab turnout swings far more than Jewish turnout, from 44.6% in 2021 to 64.8% in 2020, and it responds to list configuration, perceived influence, local candidates and backlash against exclusion. Crime is the top issue (53-80% depending on the survey), 77% back an Arab party joining the coalition, and the CEC's move to disqualify both Arab lists, overturned by the Supreme Court on 2 October, may lift turnout. Women and young voters hold most of the upside.
segments.approach: Change-bloc lists should run no GOTV of their own here. Turnout work belongs to Arab lists, local leaders and Arab civil-society coalitions, which have targeted low-turnout towns door to door before; the bloc's job is to keep its own messaging from depressing Arab turnout and, where lawful, to support those efforts transparently. Under the formation model, each 10,000 extra Joint List votes adds about 0.75 points to the chance of denying Netanyahu 61 and costs about 0.41 points of the chance of a change-led government (for Ra'am, +0.82 and -0.03). Campaign leadership must decide how much weight the blocking objective gets before allocating any resources.
segments.message: Personal security and an end to crime, concrete plans on housing, jobs and services, and real influence over the next government.
segments.messenger: Arab-list activists, mayors, local and clan leaders and civil-society volunteers, all in Arabic. Arab women and young organisers should lead contact with women and young voters.
segments.avoid: Avoid any change-bloc rhetoric that paints reliance on Arab votes as illegitimate, and never publicise turnout surges in Arab towns. Likud plans to use the CEC's station turnout releases to repeat its 2015 message about Arab turnout, and visible threat narratives mobilise the other side.

segments.role: The highest-efficiency turnout engine on the map, carrying real uncertainty about how the Druze vote will break in 2026.
segments.who: 18 Druze and Circassian localities hold 96,043 eligible voters, 1.4% of the electorate, and 6.4% of the bloc's change-government potential. Turnout was 48.5% in 2022, against 77-79% in 1996-99, and change-bloc predecessors took 68% of the vote. Beit Jann (87% projected change) and Daliyat al-Karmel (74%) yield 7.2 and 5.1 net votes per 1,000 contacts, against 2.7 in Tel Aviv.
segments.moves: Druze voting is utilitarian and candidate-driven; a party with a Druze candidate in a winnable slot usually wins that candidate's home village, often 30-50 points above its Druze average, and Blue and White won 78% in Daliyat al-Karmel in September 2019. The open grievances are Kaminitz-law fines and demolitions, the planning shortage and the Nation-State Law. One expert suggests Israel's 2025 moves to protect Druze in Sweida may pull some voters toward Netanyahu, and no 2026 Druze poll exists.
segments.approach: Run in-community GOTV first in the change-majority villages of Beit Jann, Daliyat al-Karmel, Isfiya, Kisra-Sumei, Julis and Yanuh-Jat, where turnout sits in the 30-55% band in which contact works best. In Yarka (31% projected Netanyahu bloc) and Maghar, where Arab lists take most of the vote, work only the polling stations the model marks positive. Commission a quick Druze poll before committing heavy resources, and confirm any transport plan with election counsel.
segments.message: Planning and zoning relief, a freeze on Kaminitz-law enforcement and equality under the Nation-State Law, stated as concrete commitments. Former National Unity voters need a viable-vote message, since Blue and White polls about 0.6% and a vote for it is likely lost.
segments.messenger: Druze figures with winnable list slots, led by Yashar's Kamil Abu Rokon if his slot is confirmed as winnable, plus local notables and family networks.
segments.avoid: Do not message Druze villages as part of the Arab sector, and do not rely on national messaging. Do not over-invest before the vote direction is checked, since post-Sweida movement and candidate effects can swing these villages by double digits.

segments.role: An opposition stronghold where the bloc runs no field turnout work and only token persuasion.
segments.who: 28 localities classed as Haredi hold 378,343 eligible voters; turnout was 75% in 2022 and the Netanyahu bloc took 96%. Bnei Brak (115,586 eligible) and Beit Shemesh (78,064) are the largest, and Modi'in Illit, Beitar Illit and El'ad vote at 81-84%. The segment also includes mixed cities such as Netivot, Safed and Giv'at Ze'ev, where change lists project 17-19%.
segments.moves: UTJ already mobilises about 95% of its potential electorate, and 97% of Haredi voters backed the coalition parties in 2022. The draft crisis is straining the sector. UTJ's chairman fears lower turnout, a new Haredi Public list splits the vote, and Shas is losing traditional voters to Otzma, Likud and Yashar.
segments.approach: Run no GOTV, since every extra vote here nets the Netanyahu bloc. The model scales persuasion to 15% of normal and finds 16 net votes at saturation. Limit work to quiet phone persuasion of traditional voters leaving Shas and to any non-Haredi polling stations the model marks positive in mixed cities such as Beit Shemesh and Safed.
segments.message: Where contact happens, talk to traditional voters about equal burden and cost of living, with clear respect for religious life.
segments.messenger: Observant, traditional messengers known in the community. Secular change-bloc activists should stay out.
segments.avoid: Avoid visible campaigning in Haredi neighbourhoods and draft rhetoric that reads as an attack on Haredim, since both invite counter-mobilisation. Never run activity aimed at lowering anyone's turnout.

segments.role: A persuasion battleground and the fifth-largest single prize, where turf must be chosen polling station by polling station.
segments.who: Jerusalem has 432,125 eligible voters and turned out 62% in 2022, when the Netanyahu bloc took 77% and change-bloc predecessors 20%. The model projects 24% change and 72% Netanyahu bloc, with about 6,300 persuadable and 2,900 wasted-vote rescue voters. It ranks fifth by potential (156 net votes), though efficiency is low at 0.8 net votes per 1,000 contacts.
segments.moves: Haredi, national-religious, traditional and secular neighbourhoods behave like separate electorates, and turnout rose in right-wing strongholds, Jerusalem among them, in 2022. Traditional and moderate religious voters respond to equal burden in the draft, October 7 accountability and security competence. Young secular voters in the city centre are moved by the draft (26%) and the October 7 inquiry (22%).
segments.approach: Split the city by polling station. Run GOTV only in stations where change lists lead, mainly secular and student areas. Persuasion supplies 44% of the city's potential, so run persuasion conversations in traditional and mixed neighbourhoods. Deliver wasted-vote appeals to Blue and White and Reservists voters before poll publication stops on Friday 23 October.
segments.message: Security competence and equal burden for traditional and moderate religious voters, framed around unity and a broad government. Draft and October 7 accountability for secular young voters.
segments.messenger: Right-credentialed figures such as Eisenkot and Bennett, Yashar's religious-Zionist team under Matan Kahana, and reservists. Left-coded branding belongs only in secular base stations.
segments.avoid: Avoid citywide GOTV, which nets Netanyahu-bloc votes at a 72-24 projected split. Avoid any visible activity in Haredi neighbourhoods that could trigger counter-mobilisation.

segments.role: A turnout engine of many small, reliably change-voting communities that still turn out below their potential.
segments.who: 255 kibbutzim hold 143,238 eligible voters, 2.1% of the electorate, and 5.5% of the bloc's change-government potential; the model projects change lists at 78%, against 83% for change-bloc predecessors in 2022. Turnout was 70% and stayed flat in 2022 while right-wing strongholds rose. Kibbutzim turn out about 4 points below comparable localities with the same socio-economic profile.
segments.moves: October 7 hit kibbutz communities directly; Be'eri, Nir Oz and Kfar Aza remain largely displaced, and border communities in the north were evacuated. October 7 accountability, the draft and the stakes of this election drive the base, and 60% of centre-left voters call it the most important election ever.
segments.approach: Many kibbutzim vote above 70%, where the model halves the turnout lift per contact, so efficiency is moderate and the lowest-turnout communities and members come first. Mobilise through relational organising, with members contacting members through kibbutz movement and regional networks and community WhatsApp groups. Add a vote plan to every contact, help displaced members plan travel to their registered polling station, and check whether the CEC will open special stations for evacuees. Give the 3,700 Blue and White and Reservists voters here a wasted-vote appeal before poll publication stops on 23 October.
segments.message: Use competitive, high-stakes framing. The 2022 result turned on about 30,000 votes and on lists that missed the threshold, while kibbutz turnout stayed flat. Tie the ask to October 7 accountability and equal burden.
segments.messenger: Fellow members, friends and family, plus trusted regional and movement figures.
segments.avoid: Do not assume the base will turn out by itself, and do not spend on persuasion. Keep change-list rivalry out of kibbutz contact, since moving votes between change lists adds no seats.

segments.role: The main turnout engine, holding 39% of the bloc's field potential and the largest pool of wasted-vote rescue voters.
segments.who: 45 secular, high-SES cities hold 1.36 million eligible voters and turned out 67% in 2022; change lists project 62% against 32% for the Netanyahu bloc. Tel Aviv alone (447,576 eligible, 60% turnout) holds about 805 net votes, 18% of the national total, followed by Ramat Gan, Herzliya, Kfar Saba and Givatayim. Efficiency is moderate because turnout already sits high, at 2.7 net votes per 1,000 contacts in Tel Aviv and 1.1-1.8 elsewhere.
segments.moves: Turnout barely moved here in 2022 (Tel Aviv +0.4 points) while it jumped in right-leaning cities, and the bloc's working target is above 76% turnout among its supporters in the Sharon, Tel Aviv and Haifa. Opposition supporters now say they are more certain to vote than coalition supporters (80% vs 72%). Young secular voters are moved by the draft (26%) and the October 7 inquiry (22%), and 31,000 voters here lean to Blue and White or the Reservists list, both below the threshold.
segments.approach: Select turf at polling-station (kalpi) level, since southern Tel Aviv neighbourhoods vote differently from the north and centre, and run GOTV only in stations with a clear change majority. Concentrate live contact in the last 7-10 days through volunteer doors and phones and relational texting, with a vote plan in every conversation, which matters most for young people living alone. Send one or two SMS reminders 1-3 days before 27 October, and remind supporters registered at another address, often their parents', to travel there on the free intercity buses and trains that run from 20:00 on 26 October.
segments.message: Use competitive framing. Meretz missed the threshold by about 4,000 votes in 2022, and the bloc lost by about 30,000. Tell Blue and White and Reservists voters that a vote below the threshold is lost, before poll publication stops on 23 October.
segments.messenger: Volunteers, and above all friends and family through relational asks. Together and Democrats activists lead here, since Yashar deliberately stays out of Tel Aviv.
segments.avoid: Avoid public boasts about high turnout, which Likud plans to use to rally its base, and biggest-party appeals that could sink an ally. Do not chase raw low turnout in emigrant-heavy areas, where many registered voters now live abroad.

segments.role: A secondary target where the value sits in a few Jewish polling stations and the Arab stations follow the blocking-partner logic.
segments.who: Six mixed Jewish-Arab cities hold 219,177 eligible voters and turned out 60% in 2022, when the Netanyahu bloc took 56%, Arab lists 21% and change-bloc predecessors 21%. Lod (58,888 eligible) and Ramla (57,383) project 24% change against 53-56% for the Netanyahu bloc, while Nof HaGalil (36% vs 33%) and Ma'alot-Tarshiha (35% vs 39%) are closer. The segment holds 60 net votes toward a change-led government and 368 toward blocking.
segments.moves: The Jewish parts of Lod, Ramla and Akko are among the most right-leaning large-city electorates, while the Russian-speaking Jewish neighbourhoods of Nof HaGalil and Ma'alot-Tarshiha are Yisrael Beytenu ground. Arab voters split by city, with Balad strong in Lod and Hadash-Ta'al in Akko and Nof HaGalil, and crime dominates their concerns.
segments.approach: Work strictly at polling-station level. Run Yisrael Beytenu-led persuasion and selective GOTV in Russian-speaking stations of Nof HaGalil and Ma'alot-Tarshiha, run persuasion only in right-leaning Jewish stations of Lod and Ramla, and leave Arab stations to Arab lists and civil society. Staff polling committees and observers fully, because the Netanyahu bloc has placed observers at scale before.
segments.message: Personal security, crime and cost of living for everyone. For Russian-speaking voters, add religion-and-state fairness, including civil marriage and the draft.
segments.messenger: Russian-speaking Yisrael Beytenu activists working in Russian, local Jewish community figures for persuasion, and Arab community organisers in Arab neighbourhoods.
segments.avoid: Avoid citywide GOTV, which nets Netanyahu-bloc votes in Lod and Ramla. Avoid material that sets Jewish and Arab residents against each other, since mixed cities are where station turnout releases are most likely to feed a threat narrative.

segments.role: Middle Israel's swing cities, where persuasion and turnout both pay and polling-station selection decides which one to use.
segments.who: 13 large central and coastal cities hold 981,121 eligible voters and turned out 66% in 2022; the model projects a dead heat at 47% change and 47% Netanyahu bloc. The segment holds 17% of the bloc's potential (747 net votes), split 45% GOTV, 27% persuasion and 28% wasted-vote rescue, with 18,200 persuadable and 17,400 rescue voters. Haifa (263 net votes, 52% change) is a turnout engine, while Rishon LeZion, Petah Tikva, Rehovot and Rosh HaAyin are persuasion battlegrounds.
segments.moves: These cities track the national result most closely, and pluralities flip here, as in Rishon LeZion and Rosh HaAyin in 2019-20 when Likud mobilised its voters. The swing voters are traditional non-religious and secular Likud voters; the traditional non-religious split 46% Likud to about 31% Yesh Atid and National Unity in 2022. Centrist voters rank the economy (40.5%) and the draft (34%) first, and undecided voters want cost-of-living relief and less polarisation.
segments.approach: Split each city by polling station. Run GOTV in change-majority stations such as Haifa's centre-left Jewish neighbourhoods, where the bloc targets above 76% supporter turnout, and run persuasion conversations in balanced and Likud-leaning stations along Route 4, where Yashar already campaigns. Message-test soft-right framings online before paid spend, and put paid media into the final 5-7 days.
segments.message: Lead with competence, cost of living and equal burden in the draft, framed around unity and a broad government that includes the centre-right. Concrete information about Eisenkot's and Bennett's records persuades better than attacks on Netanyahu, whom every voter already knows.
segments.messenger: Right-credentialed messengers such as Eisenkot, Bennett, Liberman and reservists for soft-right voters, with neighbours and local volunteers at the door.
segments.avoid: Avoid untargeted GOTV in Likud-leaning neighbourhoods, which Likud's own drive targets and where extra turnout nets Netanyahu-bloc votes, and keep left-coded messengers out of persuasion turf. In politically mixed households, limit GOTV contact to confirmed supporters, since partisan turnout appeals spread to other household members.

segments.role: A secondary target of hundreds of small communities, where change-majority moshavim are turnout targets and traditional moshavim are light persuasion ground.
segments.who: 454 moshavim and rural communities hold 250,807 eligible voters and turned out 73% in 2022; change lists project 58% against 38% for the Netanyahu bloc. The segment holds 6% of the bloc's potential (261 net votes). It splits sharply, from Kfar Vitkin (84% projected change) and Karmei Yosef (78%) to Shetulim (32%) and Sha'ar Efraim (47%).
segments.moves: Education, religiosity and income sort these communities more than origin does. Traditional moshavim are open to the draft wedge, since 60% of reservists would consider abandoning a party that backs exemption, and the segment holds about 6,400 Blue and White and Reservists voters.
segments.approach: Use phone and relational contact through community WhatsApp groups and local committees, because driving between small communities makes door work costly. Run GOTV only in change-majority communities and persuasion in balanced traditional moshavim. Give rescue voters a viable-vote appeal before poll publication stops on 23 October.
segments.message: Equal burden in the draft and reserve duty, security competence and cost of living. A vote below the threshold is lost.
segments.messenger: Neighbours and community members, local council figures and reservists from the community.
segments.avoid: Do not run GOTV in Netanyahu-majority moshavim. Do not read low home turnout in soldier-heavy communities as headroom, since double-envelope votes are counted elsewhere.

segments.role: The largest persuasion battleground, where untargeted GOTV backfires because Likud's own turnout drive targets these towns.
segments.who: 34 development towns and peripheral cities hold 1.25 million eligible voters and turned out 63% in 2022; the Netanyahu bloc projects 59% against 38% for change lists. The segment holds the most persuadable voters on the map (24,100) and 12% of the bloc's potential (547 net votes), of which persuasion supplies 49%, rescue 35% and GOTV 16%. Netanya, Holon, Be'er Sheva and Hadera are the biggest prizes, and Kiryat Motzkin (52% change) and Kiryat Bialik (51%) are two of the few places where change lists lead.
segments.moves: Only 58% of 2022 Likud voters said in May they would definitely vote Likud again, and those considering a switch cite October 7 (37%) and the draft (23%). Shas is losing traditional voters to Otzma, Likud and Yashar, Likud's share in Kiryat Shmona fell from 58% in 2020 to 49% in 2022, and 65% of northerners say the state is abandoning the north. Likud is betting on low-turnout stations where it won about half the vote at about 35% turnout, which it values at 2-3 seats.
segments.approach: Lead with persuasion conversations with soft Likud and traditional voters, using pre-identified lists and message-tested scripts. Run GOTV only in polling stations the model marks positive, such as change-majority stations in Kiryat Motzkin and Kiryat Bialik. Build on Yashar's local campaign structures in towns such as Dimona and Kiryat Bialik, and use place-based messages about neglect, rebuilding and jobs.
segments.message: Lead with October 7 accountability, security competence and equal burden in the draft, with respect for voters' past Likud loyalty. More voters trust an Eisenkot-led government than Netanyahu to fix the October 7 failures (48% vs 30%). Add local themes of neglect, rebuilding and cost of living.
segments.messenger: Right-credentialed messengers, including Eisenkot and Yashar's local organisers, Liberman for Russian-speaking residents, reservists and trusted local figures. Candidates add little at the door.
segments.avoid: Avoid generic GOTV, which nets Netanyahu-bloc votes here and helps Likud's Golden Clusters drive, and avoid attacks on Netanyahu or Likud voters, which harden his supporters. Do not read very low turnout in places like central Eilat or Netanya's hotel strip as headroom, since much of it reflects non-resident registration.

segments.role: An opposition stronghold with one narrow persuasion opening among moderate religious-Zionists in mixed suburbs.
segments.who: 104 religious-Zionist communities inside the Green Line hold 77,800 eligible voters; turnout was 77% in 2022 and the Netanyahu bloc took 82%. Givat Shmuel (20,150 eligible, 40% projected change) and Hosha'aya (41%) are Secondary targets, while Yad Binyamin, Nof Ayalon and Bareket project 12-16% change.
segments.moves: Religious-Zionist voters moved right between 2019 and 2022, and an early-September Dialog poll put Yashar and Together at about 7% combined in the sector, with security (35%) and Jewish identity (25%) ahead of the draft (15%). Yashar aims for about two more seats from traditional and moderate religious-Zionist voters through a headquarters under Matan Kahana covering Givat Shmuel, Efrat and Gush Etzion. Among religious reservists, 35% would consider dropping a party that backs draft exemption.
segments.approach: Run no GOTV. Support Yashar's existing religious-Zionist operation with targeted persuasion conversations in Givat Shmuel and Hosha'aya-type mixed communities through reservist networks, and coordinate so the change lists do not duplicate effort. The model scales persuasion to 60% of normal here and finds 31 net votes at saturation, so keep the investment small.
segments.message: Security competence, shared service and equal burden, and respect for Jewish identity, framed around a broad national government.
segments.messenger: Religious-Zionist figures such as Matan Kahana, religious reservists and local community members.
segments.avoid: Avoid secular or left-coded messengers and religion-and-state attacks that read as hostile to religious life. Run no turnout work.

segments.role: A persuasion battleground with turnout pockets, where Yisrael Beytenu carries the bloc's case to Russian-speaking ex-Likud voters.
segments.who: 10 Russian-speaking towns hold 580,965 eligible voters and turned out 59% in 2022; the Netanyahu bloc projects 56% against 41% for change lists. The segment holds 264 net votes, split about 40% persuasion, 31% GOTV and 28% rescue. Ashdod (181,784 eligible, 35% change), Bat Yam (51% turnout, 45% change) and Ashkelon lead by size, while Karmiel (52%) and Nesher (54%) have change majorities.
segments.moves: Russian speakers are about 15% of the population, largely secular, hawkish on security and open to religion-and-state messages; 1990s adult immigrants lean right, and the Israeli-born generation votes like other Israelis. Yisrael Beytenu has mapped the neighbourhoods and polling stations where Likud did best and is concentrating on Russian-speaking ex-Likud voters. The research desk found no 2026 poll of Russian speakers, so the model leans on past results.
segments.approach: Work at polling-station level. Run GOTV in Russian-speaking stations where change lists lead, especially in Karmiel, Nesher, Kiryat Yam and Bat Yam, and run persuasion in Russian-speaking, Likud-leaning stations in Ashdod and Ashkelon. Contact must be in Russian and by Russian-speaking volunteers, with separate messages and messengers for the Mizrahi and Russian-speaking communities of the same town.
segments.message: Religion-and-state fairness, including civil marriage and equal burden in the draft, plus security competence and cost of living.
segments.messenger: Liberman and Yisrael Beytenu's Russian-speaking activists, Russian-language media and community figures.
segments.avoid: Avoid Hebrew-only material and untargeted GOTV in Ashdod and Ashkelon, where the Netanyahu bloc projects 58-62%. Discount raw low turnout, which partly reflects emigrants and elderly residents.

segments.role: An opposition stronghold with no field work beyond Yashar's existing religious-Zionist outreach.
segments.who: 82 national-religious West Bank settlements hold 101,984 eligible voters; turnout was 75% in 2022 and the Netanyahu bloc took 91%. Efrat (7,945 eligible, 26% projected change) is the largest, and Kiryat Arba (15%) and Beit El (11%) sit near the bottom. The model finds no positive GOTV turf and 22 net votes at saturation.
segments.moves: RZP took about 60% of the vote east of the separation barrier in 2022, and security and Jewish identity lead the sector's concerns. Yashar's Kahana-led headquarters covers Efrat and Gush Etzion. Soldiers' double-envelope votes are counted away from home, so recorded turnout understates real turnout.
segments.approach: Run no GOTV and no change-bloc field operation. Leave the narrow opening in Efrat and Gush Etzion to Yashar's religious-Zionist team, which can use phone and relational contact with identified moderates.
segments.message: Security competence, equal burden and a broad national government that respects religious life.
segments.messenger: Religious-Zionist figures and local residents connected to Yashar's operation.
segments.avoid: Avoid visible secular campaigning, which can provoke counter-mobilisation. Never treat low recorded turnout as headroom.

segments.role: A secondary target with a few change-majority communities near the Green Line and persuasion ground in Ariel and Ma'ale Adumim.
segments.who: 32 secular and mixed West Bank localities hold 78,737 eligible voters and turned out 70% in 2022; the Netanyahu bloc projects 57% against 40% for change lists. Ma'ale Adumim (28,142 eligible, 28% projected change) and Ariel (43%) are the largest, while Har Adar (64%), Kfar HaOranim (70%), Oranit (52%) and Alfei Menashe (50%) lean change.
segments.moves: Secular settlements west of the barrier are Likud and Yisrael Beytenu territory, and Ariel was on Likud's 2022 final-day turnout list. Yashar's religious-Zionist headquarters covers Ariel, and the draft is a strong wedge with right-leaning reservist communities.
segments.approach: Run GOTV only in change-majority communities such as Har Adar, Kfar HaOranim, Oranit and Alfei Menashe, using relational contact. Run persuasion through Yisrael Beytenu and Yashar in Ariel and Ma'ale Adumim. The whole segment is worth about 41 net votes, so keep the effort proportionate.
segments.message: Security competence, equal burden in the draft and reserve duty, and cost of living.
segments.messenger: Yisrael Beytenu and Yashar local activists, reservists and residents.
segments.avoid: Avoid citywide GOTV in Ariel and Ma'ale Adumim, where the Netanyahu bloc leads and Likud mobilises. Do not read low home turnout in soldier-heavy communities as headroom.
